title: Microcohort Triage Decision Grid (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
- Draft a compact decision grid & runbook for human-triaged microcohort canaries that balances quality, latency, and cost.
- Focus: short-lived canaries for LLM behavior changes (prompt tweak, model variant, quantization) where rapid human checks + automated gates reduce blast radius.

Scope / When to use this pattern:
- New prompt templates with >10% downstream UI exposure.
- Model weight swap or quantized variant rollout with unknown tail-latency behavior.
- Reranker / rerank/embedding changes that could materially shift results.
- NOT intended for large-scale infra-only deploys (use standard staged rollout).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Create 3 microcohorts (canary-0 small synthetic, canary-1 real-sample, canary-2 representative slice).
- Run 48h tight telemetry window with 15m signal checks.
- Automated gates on latency, 95p latency, token-cost, and hallucination proxy (QA mismatch rate).
- Human triage if any composite signal trips.

Key definitions (working):
- Microcohort: ~0.1-2% of traffic constrained by user attributes or synthetic injection.
- Hallucination proxy: task-specific classifier + human spot-check false-positive rate.
- Cost gate: token-per-response uplift beyond baseline for same slice.

Decision grid (operational):
Rows = Signals, Columns = Severity bands (green / amber / red) + immediate action.
Signals: latency_p50, latency_p95, infra_errors(5xx), model_errors(exceptions), token_cost_per_response, qa_mismatch_rate, distribution_shift_score, coverage_drop (e.g., embeddings fewer hits).

- latency_p50:
  - green: <= baseline + 5ms -> continue
  - amber: baseline + 5-30ms -> monitor, reduce weight for next 1h if amber persists
  - red: > baseline + 30ms or sustained p95 surge -> rollback canary and page SRE

- latency_p95:
  - green: <= baseline + 20ms -> continue
  - amber: +20-100ms -> slow-down rollout, enable fallback
  - red: > +100ms -> immediate rollback and incident post-mortem

- infra_errors (5xx):
  - green: <0.1%
  - amber: 0.1-1% -> throttle, notify infra owner, escalate if persists 30m
  - red: >1% -> rollback, page SRE

- token_cost_per_response (relative):
  - green: <=+3%
  - amber: +3-15% -> auto-reduce exposure to next slice; flag finance if sustained 24h
  - red: >+15% -> rollback or force quantized fallback

- qa_mismatch_rate (behavior quality proxy):
  - green: within historical variance
  - amber: +small uplift (0.5-3%) -> human-reviewed sample (50 examples/interval)
  - red: >3% -> pause rollout; organize immediate triage session w/ product + ML

- distribution_shift_score (embedding drift / input feature changes):
  - green: within baseline
  - amber: small shift -> increase synthetic tests, hold expansion
  - red: big shift -> rollback and deeper data investigation

Escalation matrix (roles + timelines):
- Canary owner (usually PM/PMM): initial triage, coordinate humans, update stakeholders (0-15m)
- ML lead: investigate model-specific causes, propose mitigation (15-60m)
- Infra/SRE on-call: confirm infra vs model (15-60m), perform rollback if infra implicated
- Product engineering: patch prompt/heuristics, prepare hotfix route (60-180m)
- Ops / Finance contact: if cost gate triggers sustained amber >24h -> assess cost cap

Human-in-loop triage checklist (first 60m):
- Confirm signal: check raw traces, top-k examples for failure class
- Quick A/B sanity: sample pairs across canary & baseline 50/50 blind check
- Reproduce locally with saved request and model variant (if reproducible -> bug)
- If hallucination-related: collect 100 examples, annotate 10 fast-fail cases and escalate
- Decide: continue (monitor), throttle (reduce exposure by factor), rollback, or block further slices

Microcohort construction heuristics (practical rules):
- synthetic microcohort (canary-0): injected requests from synthetic harness; useful to validate deterministic regressions quickly
- narrow real-sample (canary-1): high-value customers subset or geographic cluster with low churn risk
- representative slice (canary-2): random stratified sample by product segment (match production distribution)
- Keep cohorts orthogonal where possible to isolate drivers (e.g., device type vs region).

Weighting schedule (example):
- Phase 0 (smoke): 0.02% synthetic, 15m observation
- Phase 1 (narrow real): 0.2% real-sample, 1h observation (requires human sign-off to expand)
- Phase 2 (rep slice): 1% stratified, 6-24h observation depending on signal noise
- Phase 3 (ramp): 5-25% progressive ramp with automated SLO gates

Telemetry / dashboards to surface (must be live, 15m buckets):
- Request volume and per-cohort breakdown
- p50/p95/p99 latency per model variant and per-route
- Error rates (5xx, model exceptions) per cohort
- Token cost per response and normalized cost delta vs baseline
- Hallucination proxy: QA classifier + human-annotated spot checks (expose sample list)
- Distribution shift histograms (embedding cosine mean, token length distribution)
- Top-10 failing prompts / top-10 stack traces

Automated controls / ops knobs we require (implementation notes):
- Traffic split controller with immediate rollback boolean + scheduled decay
- Cost cap circuit breaker: global and per-customer thresholds
- Quick-snapshot saves of request/response + model state for triage (privacy-safe hash)
- Canary weight ramp rollbacks if composite signal crosses composite threshold (e.g., any 2 amber in 30m => auto-throttle)

A/B design notes (for LLM features):
- Use paired evaluations when possible: present baseline vs canary outputs side-by-side to human raters to reduce noise
- Blind labeling pipeline: ensure we hide model names/weights from reviewers
- If measuring business metric (CTR, conversion), keep sufficient sample size for token-cost vs value tradeoff estimation
- Pre-register primary/secondary metrics and buckets before expansion

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (TODO):
- How long to keep synthetic vs real microcohorts before mixing signals? (current default 48h but needs calibration)
- QA classifier sensitivity tuning: how to avoid false positives that block valid rollouts?
- Should cost cap be absolute dollars or relative to historical per-route spend? (suggest relative by default)
- Privacy constraints on snapshotting request/response for triage — need legal review for EU customers

Immediate next steps (action items):
- (Priya) schedule 30m sync w/ SRE + ML infra to confirm instrumentation and rollback API (by 2025-01-22)
- (Ethan) prototype composite gate that counts amber signals across 15m windows (by 2025-01-29)
- (Ava) draft human-rating guideline + sample selection script for paired evals (by 2025-01-24)
- (Samir) cost-cap config options: per-route relative, global hard cap, and per-customer soft cap (PR draft 78)

Notes / rough meeting fragment (raw):
- "if we auto-throttle too aggressively we lose signal — need smarter decay schedule"
- "synthetic injection helped catch the token-cost regression last week before real users saw it"
- "can we add small jitter to p95 checks to avoid flapping?"

References & related:
- See: linked artifact JIRA-ENG-2314 (instrumentation spec)
- Quick-read: rollout economics primer (confluence: /display/RWI/Rollout+Economics)

End of draft — heavy WIP. Keep short iterations, please add comments inline.
